mainTopic: שמאי's protest and the בית חורון gift rule, the greatness of הלל's students, and a new משנה on believing a man about his son or brother
overview: The amud opens as יונתן בן עוזיאל finishes his answer to שמאי. A man had given יונתן his property to keep it away from his sons, and יונתן gave part of it back to them. יונתן argues that if his sale and his dedication to the מקדש stand, his return to the sons stands too, and שמאי admits defeat. The גמרא explains that שמאי had relied on the case of בית חורון. There, a son gave a courtyard and a meal to a friend only so his vowing father could attend a wedding. From that case the חכמים ruled that a gift the receiver cannot dedicate is not a real gift. Since יונתן came up, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about the eighty students of הלל. Even the smallest of them, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, mastered every area of Torah, and birds flying over the greatest, יונתן בן עוזיאל, were burned while he learned. A new משנה then teaches that a man is believed when he says 'this is my son,' but not when he says 'this is my brother,' except from his own share. The גמרא begins by explaining that 'this is my son' is believed so that the son inherits him and his wife is exempt from יבום.

steps.title: יונתן finishes his defense: what I returned stands
steps.stepSummary: יונתן בן עוזיאל ends his argument. If שמאי cannot undo the sale and the dedication, he cannot undo the part given back to the sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if not, you cannot take back what I returned.
steps.whatsHappening: יונתן בן עוזיאל is finishing his answer to שמאי's protest. If his sale and his dedication are valid, then his return of the property to the sons is valid too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three of יונתן's actions came from the same ownership. Selling and dedicating to the מקדש show that he was the full owner. So no one can single out the return to the sons as fake or invalid while letting the other two stand.

keyTerms.meaning: If not
To take back, to undo someone's possession
That I returned (to the sons)

phrases.english: But if not, you cannot
take back what I returned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם לָאו – אִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיא מַה שֶּׁהֶחְזַרְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes יונתן's answer to שמאי's protest, which began on the previous page
steps.terutzResolutionType: Consistency argument: all of an owner's acts stand or fall together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמאי thought the return to the sons could be undone
steps.terutzMaskana: The return is as valid as the sale and the dedication

steps.title: שמאי admits defeat
steps.stepSummary: שמאי says twice that בן עוזיאל has defeated him in argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Ben Uzziel has defeated me! Ben Uzziel has defeated me!
steps.whatsHappening: שמאי accepts יונתן's argument and admits he has no answer to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying it twice shows how strongly שמאי concedes. This closes the story, but it leaves open why שמאי protested in the first place, and the גמרא asks about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: He struck back at me, he defeated me in argument
יונתן בן עוזיאל, a great student of הלל

phrases.english: He said: Ben Uzziel has defeated me!
Ben Uzziel has defeated me!

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: יונתן's handling of the gift stands, and שמאי withdraws his protest
steps.whatToRemember: יונתן won because he had truly acted as an owner. He sold and dedicated property, and no one can undo those acts.

steps.title: What was שמאי thinking at first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמאי protested in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he hold at the beginning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what reasoning led שמאי to object before he was defeated. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though שמאי gave in, a great sage would not have protested without a reason. The גמרא wants to find the source he was relying on.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, from the beginning
What did he hold, what was his reasoning

phrases.english: What did he hold at the beginning?
phrases.notes: 'He' is שמאי, before he gave in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at שמאי's original position after his concession
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for שמאי's original protest against יונתן

steps.title: Because of the incident in בית חורון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמאי was relying on a known case from בית חורון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the incident in בית חורון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer: שמאי was thinking of the case of בית חורון. It will now quote that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בית חורון case, the rabbis treated a gift given only to get around a prohibition as not a real gift. שמאי thought the father's gift to יונתן was the same kind of gift. Its only purpose was to keep the property away from the sons, so it was not a real gift that יונתן could do with as he pleased, such as giving it back to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of
An incident, a real case that happened
בית חורון, a town in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Because of the incident of בית חורון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about שמאי's reasoning
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמאי based his protest on the בית חורון precedent, where a gift made only as a trick was not treated as a real gift
steps.confusionAlert: Remember what שמאי was worried about. He did not say the father's gift was impossible. He thought it was not a full gift, because it was given to יונתן only to keep the property away from the sons. So in his view יונתן had no right to give part of it back to them.

steps.title: The case: a son gives his courtyard and meal to a friend for his father's sake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. A man whose father was forbidden by a vow to benefit from him gave his courtyard and wedding meal to a friend, so that his father could come to the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: There was an incident in בית חורון with a man whose father was forbidden by a vow to benefit from him. He was marrying off his son, and he said to his friend: The courtyard and the meal are given to you as a gift, but they are yours only so that my father will come and eat with us at the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the בית חורון case. A son tries to get around his father's vow by giving the courtyard and meal to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father could not benefit from anything belonging to his son. So the son transferred ownership to a friend, hoping the father would be eating the friend's food. But the son openly attached a purpose to the gift, and that already hints the gift is not truly complete.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Forbidden by a vow to benefit
Marrying off
As a gift

phrases.english: As we learned: There was an incident in בית חורון,
with a man whose father
was forbidden by a vow to benefit from him,
and he was marrying off his son;
and he said to his friend:
The courtyard and the meal
are given to you as a gift,
but they are yours only
so that my father will come
and eat with us at the meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that step 4 referred to
steps.raayaObject: שמאי's suspicion that a gift with a hidden purpose is not a real gift
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נדרים about the incident in בית חורון

steps.title: The friend dedicates everything, and the son protests
steps.stepSummary: The friend says that if the gift is really his, he dedicates it all to the מקדש. The son objects that he did not give it for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If they are mine, they are hereby dedicated to Heaven! He said to him: I did not give you what is mine so that you should dedicate them to Heaven!
steps.whatsHappening: The friend tests whether the gift is real by dedicating it to the מקדש. The son's angry reaction shows he never meant to give it away for real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A true owner may do anything with his property, including dedicate it. The son's protest shows he still thought of the property as his own. In his mind, the 'gift' was only a tool for getting his father to the meal.

keyTerms.meaning: Dedicated to the מקדש (הקדש)
To Heaven, meaning to the מקדש
That you should dedicate them

phrases.english: He said to him: If they are mine,
they are hereby dedicated to Heaven!

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: לֹא נָתַתִּי לְךָ אֶת שֶׁלִּי
phrases.english: He said to him: I did not give you what is mine
so that you should dedicate them to Heaven!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אִם שֶׁלִּי הֵן – הֲרֵי הֵן מוּקְדָּשִׁין לַשָּׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the בית חורון case
steps.raayaObject: That a gift given for a hidden purpose is not a real gift
steps.raayaSupportSource: The son's objection reveals that he never truly gave up ownership

steps.title: The friend exposes the gift as a trick
steps.stepSummary: The friend replies that the gift was only meant to let father and son eat together and make peace, while the sin of breaking the vow would fall on the friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You gave me what is yours only so that you and your father would eat and drink and make peace with each other, and the sin would hang on my head!
steps.whatsHappening: The friend explains why he dedicated the property. The gift was fake, and accepting it would have made him responsible for helping the father break his vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the main point of the בית חורון case. A gift made only to get around a prohibition is not a real gift, so the vow is still being broken. This is the idea שמאי applied to the father's gift to יונתן, but יונתן had shown real ownership by selling and dedicating part of the property.

keyTerms.meaning: Making peace with each other
A sin
Hanging on his head, meaning he carries the blame

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: לֹא נָתַתָּ לִי אֶת שֶׁלְּךָ
phrases.english: He said to him: You did not give me what is yours
except so that you and your father
would eat and drink
and make peace with each other,
and the sin would hang on his head!
phrases.notes: 'His head' is a polite way of saying 'my head.' The friend means himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: לֹא נָתַתָּ לִי אֶת שֶׁלְּךָ אֶלָּא שֶׁתְּהֵא אַתָּה וְאָבִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The friend answers the son's protest, showing the gift was only a trick
steps.raayaObject: שמאי's view that the father's gift to יונתן might be a pretend gift
steps.raayaSupportSource: The בית חורון case, where a gift given only to get around a vow was treated as fake
steps.whatToRemember: A gift made only to get around a prohibition is not a real gift. שמאי used this idea, but יונתן's real acts of ownership (selling and dedicating) showed his case was different.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case is the classic source for the idea that a 'gift' which is really a trick does not count as a real transfer of ownership.

steps.title: The Sages' rule: a gift that cannot be dedicated is not a gift
steps.stepSummary: The משנה of בית חורון ends with the rule of the חכמים: any gift that the receiver could not dedicate to the מקדש is not a real gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said: any gift that is not fully the receiver's, so that if he dedicated it the dedication would work, is not a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the בית חורון משנה with the general rule the חכמים drew from that story. This rule is the source שמאי was relying on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בית חורון the friend's 'gift' was only a trick to let the father eat, so it was not truly his and he could not dedicate it. From this the חכמים set a test: a real gift must belong to the receiver so fully that he could even dedicate it to the מקדש. That is why שמאי protested about a gift that seemed to be only a cover.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift
He dedicated it to the מקדש
It becomes holy and belongs to the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The test of a real gift: could the receiver dedicate it to the מקדש? If not, it is not a gift.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule closes the proof that began in Step 4 and explains what שמאי was worried about.

phrases.english: The Sages said:
Any gift that is not such
that if he dedicated it, it would be dedicated –
is not a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: כׇּל מַתָּנָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁאִם הִקְדִּישָׁהּ מוּקְדֶּשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quoted משנה from Steps 5-7 by stating the rule that comes out of the story.
steps.raayaObject: Why שמאי protested about the gift (Step 3).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of the חכמים at the end of the בית חורון משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A gift that the receiver cannot dedicate is not a valid gift, and this is the basis of שמאי's protest.

steps.title: The eighty students of הלל הזקן
steps.stepSummary: Because יונתן בן עוזיאל came up, the גמרא brings a ברייתא describing the eighty students of הלל הזקן and their levels.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: הלל הזקן had eighty students. Thirty were worthy of the שכינה resting on them like משה רבינו. Thirty were worthy of the sun standing still for them like יהושע בן נון. Twenty were in between. The greatest was יונתן בן עוזיאל and the smallest was רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The הלכה discussion is finished, and the גמרא now moves to a story-style teaching about the students of הלל, sparked by the mention of יונתן בן עוזיאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side topic, not part of the argument about gifts. It sets up a surprising contrast: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, a giant of Torah, is called the 'smallest' of this group. That raises the question of how great the others must have been, and the next step shows just how great he was.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Hillel the Elder
The Divine Presence
In between, of a middle level

steps.confusionAlert: The order in the list does not follow the order of greatness. The twenty 'in between' stand between the other two groups: below the thirty compared to משה and above the thirty compared to יהושע.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוֹנִים תַּלְמִידִים הָיוּ לוֹ לְהִלֵּל הַזָּקֵן;
phrases.english: Hillel the Elder had eighty students;
thirty of them were worthy
that the Divine Presence should rest on them as on Moses our teacher,
thirty of them were worthy

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁתַּעֲמוֹד לָהֶן חַמָּה כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן,
phrases.english: that the sun should stand still for them as for Joshua son of Nun,
twenty were in between.
The greatest of them all was Yonatan ben Uzziel,

phrases.aramaic: קָטָן שֶׁבְּכוּלָּן – רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי.
phrases.english: the smallest of them all was Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁמוֹנִים תַּלְמִידִים הָיוּ לוֹ לְהִלֵּל הַזָּקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the halachic discussion because the story mentioned יונתן בן עוזיאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל's students were on three levels. יונתן בן עוזיאל was the greatest and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי the smallest.

steps.title: Everything רבן יוחנן בן זכאי mastered
steps.stepSummary: Even the 'smallest' student, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, did not leave out any area of Torah learning, from פסוקים to the speech of angels.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי that he did not leave out any area of learning: מקרא, משנה, תלמוד, הלכות and אגדות, the fine details of the Torah and of the סופרים, קל וחומר and גזירה שוה, calculating the seasons and גימטריאות, parables of launderers and parables of foxes, the speech of demons, of palm trees and of the ministering angels, a great matter and a small matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists all the areas of wisdom that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי mastered, to show how great even the 'smallest' student was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list starts with the basics (פסוקים, משנה), moves to the tools for learning Torah (קל וחומר, גזירה שוה, גימטריא), and then to hidden wisdom (the speech of demons, trees and angels). It ends with 'a great matter and a small matter,' which the next step will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not leave out or neglect
The fine details of the Rabbis' laws
Learning from matching words in two places in the Torah
Calculating the seasons for the calendar
Fox fables used to teach lessons

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: They said about Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
that he did not leave out Scripture and Mishnah,
Talmud, laws and stories,
fine details of the Torah and fine details of the scribes,
and kal vachomer reasoning, and gezeirah shavah comparisons,
and calculating the seasons, and number values of letters,
and parables of launderers, and parables of foxes,
the speech of demons, and the speech of palm trees,
and the speech of the ministering angels,
and a great matter, and a small matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי, שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 9 by showing how great רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was, even though he was called the 'smallest.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי mastered every area of Torah and wisdom.

steps.title: Explaining 'a great matter' and 'a small matter'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the last two items on the list: the 'great matter' is מעשה מרכבה and the 'small matter' is the discussions of אביי and רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A great matter' means מעשה מרכבה, the secrets of the Divine Chariot. 'A small matter' means the discussions of אביי and רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain two unclear phrases from the end of the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'great matter' is the deepest hidden wisdom about ה׳'s Chariot. The 'small matter' is the detailed back-and-forth of halachic reasoning. So he mastered both the highest secrets and the fine details of halacha.

keyTerms.meaning: The secrets of the Divine Chariot (יחזקאל 1)
The discussions and debates of אביי and רבא

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא lived hundreds of years after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. It means he already knew the kind of halachic questions that they would later discuss. Also, 'small' only means smaller next to the Chariot, not unimportant.

phrases.english: "A great matter" means the workings of the Divine Chariot,
"and a small matter" means the discussions of Abaye and Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last two phrases of the list in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Great matter = מעשה מרכבה. Small matter = the discussions of אביי and רבא.

steps.title: A verse: those who love Torah are filled with treasures
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's huge store of learning fulfills the פסוק in משלי that ה׳ fills the treasuries of those who love Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fulfilled what is said: "To give those who love Me an inheritance of substance, and I will fill their treasuries."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the praise of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי by tying it to a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'treasuries' in the פסוק are read as treasuries of Torah wisdom. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, who loved Torah, was filled with every kind of learning, just as the פסוק promises.

keyTerms.meaning: To fulfill what is written
To give as an inheritance
Their treasuries, their storehouses

steps.whatToRemember: Even the 'smallest' of הלל's students mastered all of Torah, from the Chariot to the debates of אביי and רבא. This fulfills the promise that ה׳ fills the treasuries of those who love Him.

phrases.english: to fulfill what is said:
"To give those who love Me an inheritance of substance,
and I will fill their treasuries."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the praise of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי with a supporting פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's complete mastery of Torah.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ה׳ fills those who love Torah with treasures of wisdom, as seen in רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

steps.title: If the smallest student was this great, the greatest was even greater
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, the 'smallest' of הלל's students, to the greatest of them: he must have been even greater.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since the smallest of them all was like this, the greatest of them all was certainly even more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a simple 'how much more so' conclusion from the praise of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. This also sets up the next story about the greatest student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was the smallest student, and Step 10 showed that he learned every area of Torah. So whoever was ranked above him must have been on an even higher level. This turns our attention to יונתן בן עוזיאל, who was named earlier as the greatest.

keyTerms.meaning: how much more so (a 'small case to big case' argument)
the smallest of them all
the greatest of them all

phrases.english: And since the smallest of them all was like this,
phrases.notes: The 'smallest' is רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, the one praised in the last few steps.

phrases.english: the greatest of them all
how much more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a 'how much more so' argument from the praise of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The greatest of הלל's students was even greater than רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

steps.title: Birds were burned when יונתן בן עוזיאל learned Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells how holy יונתן בן עוזיאל's learning was: any bird that flew over him while he learned was burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about יונתן בן עוזיאל: when he sat and learned Torah, any bird that flew over him was burned up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to show just how great יונתן בן עוזיאל, the greatest student, really was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step said the greatest student was even greater than רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. This story gives a picture of that greatness: his Torah learning carried such holiness that a bird flying overhead was burned. With this the side discussion that started from the mention of יונתן בן עוזיאל in the story with שמאי comes to an end.

keyTerms.meaning: the greatest of הלל הזקן's eighty students
busy learning Torah
a bird
was burned up

steps.whatToRemember: This ends the side discussion about הלל's students. The smallest, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, knew all of Torah, and the greatest, יונתן בן עוזיאל, learned with such holiness that birds above him were burned.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עוּזִּיאֵל,
phrases.english: They said about יונתן בן עוזיאל
that when he would sit and learn Torah,
any bird that flew over him was burned up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל יוֹנָתָן בֶּן עוּזִּיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story that shows the greatness the last step reasoned about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יונתן בן עוזיאל's Torah learning was so holy that birds flying over him were burned.

steps.title: A man is believed about 'my son' but not about 'my brother'
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a man who says 'this is my son' is believed. A man who says 'this is my brother' is not believed against his brothers, but the 'brother' takes a share from the speaker's own portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who says 'This is my son' is believed. One who says 'This is my brother' is not believed, but the man shares with him from his own portion.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with how far we believe a person who says someone is related to him, for ירושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About his son, the man is fully believed. About a brother, his word cannot force his other brothers to give up any of their father's inheritance. Still, his claim binds him, so the 'brother' gets a share out of the speaker's part.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה (the text the גמרא discusses)
believed, trusted
not believed
from his own portion

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not believed' does not mean his words are ignored. He is not believed against the other brothers, but he still has to share his own portion because of what he said.

phrases.english: MISHNA
One who says 'This is my son' is believed;
one who says 'This is my brother' is not believed,
and he takes a share with him from his portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic, after the side discussion about הלל's students ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man is believed about his son. About a brother he is not believed against the others, but he must share his own portion.

steps.title: If the 'brother' dies, the property goes back to the speaker
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: if the man called 'brother' dies, the property he got goes back to where it came from.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he dies, the property goes back to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds what happens to the share if the 'brother' dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'brother' only got property because of the speaker's own claim, and it came out of the speaker's portion. So when he dies, that property returns to the speaker and not to all the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: he died
property
shall go back to their place

phrases.english: If he dies, the property goes back to its place.
phrases.notes: 'Its place' means back to the brother who said 'this is my brother,' since it came from his portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, adding the case where the 'brother' dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the 'brother' dies, the share he took returns to the speaker.

steps.title: Property from elsewhere is shared by all the brothers
steps.stepSummary: If the 'brother' got property from some other source and then died, all of the speaker's brothers inherit it together with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If property came to him from somewhere else, his brothers inherit together with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a different kind of property: things the 'brother' got from another source, not from the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This property never came out of the speaker's portion. By the speaker's own claim, the dead man is a brother to all of them, so all the brothers share it. The speaker cannot keep it for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: came to him (literally, fell to him)
from another source
they will inherit

steps.whatToRemember: The speaker's claim works against himself, never against his brothers. What came from his portion goes back to him alone. What came from elsewhere is shared by all the brothers, because he says the dead man is their brother too.

phrases.english: If property came to him from somewhere else,
his brothers inherit together with him.
phrases.notes: 'His brothers' means the speaker's brothers. By his own claim they are brothers of the dead man too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets this case against step 16: there the property came from the speaker, here it came from somewhere else.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property the 'brother' got from another source is inherited by all the speaker's brothers together with him.

steps.title: What practical difference does 'this is my son' make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a man who says 'this is my son' is believed. It asks what legal result that has.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said that if a man says 'This is my son,' he is believed. For what law does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה. It quotes the line 'this is my son is believed' and asks what practical law this affects. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the man is נאמן but never said what he is believed about. The גמרא wants to know which real halachic results come from accepting his word. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that explains the משנה
Believed; his word is accepted
'For what law?' The גמרא is asking what practical difference something makes

phrases.english: GEMARA: 'This is my son' is believed.
For what law [is this said]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the משנה quoted in Step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which practical halachic results follow from believing a man who says 'this is my son'

steps.title: The son inherits him, and his wife is exempt from levirate marriage
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל answers that the man is believed for two things: the son inherits from him, and his wife is exempt from יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: He is believed so that the son inherits from him, and so that his wife is exempt from יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, answers the question from Step 18. He gives two practical results of believing the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the son inherits the man's property, as any son would. Second, because the man now has a child, his wife does not need יבום when he dies. Only a man who dies with no children leaves his wife needing יבום. One statement about who his son is changes both inheritance and the wife's marriage status.

keyTerms.meaning: So that he (the son) inherits from him
Levirate marriage: a man's brother marries his widow if he died with no children
To exempt; to free from an obligation

steps.whatToRemember: Saying 'this is my son' is believed for two things: the son inherits, and the wife is exempt from יבום.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'ליורשו' as the father inheriting the son. It means the son inherits from the father. The יבום exemption works because a man who leaves a child does not leave his widow needing יבום.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
For inheriting him,
and to exempt his wife from levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The man is believed so the son inherits from him and so his wife is exempt from יבום
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Believing 'this is my son' affects both inheritance and the יבום exemption
